open_points.subject: A17 startup concurrency decision referenced by A21
open_points.text: a start serving nothing until every check passed and binding each listener exclusively (A17)
open_points.question: What are A17's actual normative rules for check order, listener-binding order, atomicity across multiple listeners, failure rollback, and the exact condition under which startup is refused?
options: All checks pass before any listener is bound, then all listeners are acquired atomically or startup fails.
Listeners are bound independently after or among checks; failure releases earlier bindings and startup fails.
Each listener is acquired independently without a global startup exclusion, so concurrent starts may split the bindings and both fail.
open_points.default_guess: Run every non-binding check first, acquire all listeners without serving, release every acquired listener and refuse startup if any acquisition fails, and begin serving only after all acquisitions succeed.

witness.initial: Two Registry processes have the same valid configuration naming two listener addresses, and neither address is initially bound.
events: Process P1 completes its checks and binds listener L1.
Process P2 completes its checks and binds listener L2.
P1 attempts L2 while P2 attempts L1.
outcomes: A globally coordinated interpretation lets exactly one process acquire both listeners and serve while the other refuses startup.
A per-listener interpretation lets the processes split the listeners, causing both starts to fail and leaving Registry unavailable after rollback.
witness.observer: The owner and every caller attempting to reach Registry

open_points.subject: A21 Required tests for the newly added A17 reference
open_points.text:
Each APPLICABLE category's decisions have their own required tests, and
   those tests pass.
open_points.question: Which A17 Required tests demonstrate the startup and exclusive-listener concurrency guarantee, and what exactly must those tests show?
options: A test races two complete Registry startups and proves that at most one serves and no process serves a partial listener set.
Separate tests prove checks finish before serving, each listener is exclusively bound, and partial bindings are released on failure.
A17 has no applicable executable test and A21 must state another form of evidence.
open_points.default_guess: Require a concurrent two-process startup test that proves no process serves before all checks and bindings succeed, no listener is shared, partial acquisition is rolled back, and at most one process serves the complete configured listener set.
